name: CEoH (Contextual Evolution of Heuristics)
org: Karlsruhe Institute of Technology and TU Dortmund University
one_liner: EoH with a problem description added to every prompt, so smaller LLMs can design heuristics for niche problems.

loop.proposes: Tree-search scoring heuristics for the unit-load pre-marshalling problem, as thought plus code
loop.judged_by: Running the heuristic and measuring the average relative gap of its move count to a lower bound
loop.steers: Fitness drives EoH selection; the added problem description is kept in every prompt

headline_result: For unit-load pre-marshalling, Qwen2.5-Coder:32b with CEoH reached a fitness of 12.5% (best overall), against 14.3% for the best EoH run (GPT-4o 2024-08-06). The "Optimal A*" baseline scored about 8.1%. CEoH outperformed EoH for Gemma2:27b, Qwen2.5-Coder:32b and DeepSeekV3:685b.
caveat: One niche problem. On unseen instances fitness rose to 30.8 (Qwen CEoH) and 33.9 (GPT-4o EoH), which the authors read as overfitting. For GPT-4o EoH was better than CEoH, and none solved the hardest case (80% fill).
beyond_harness_note: An evolutionary loop over a population produces a heuristic that is plugged into a search algorithm and used without the model.
generative_model: Pretrained LLMs, frozen (Gemma2:27b, Qwen2.5-Coder:32b, DeepSeekV3:685b, GPT-4o)
algorithmic_authority: Instance evaluation of heuristic inside a tree search

sources.title: Leveraging Large Language Models to Develop Heuristics for Emerging Optimization Problems

verification.notes: Resolved arXiv:2503.03350 (Bomer, Koltermann, Disselnmeyer, Dorr, Meyer; v1 5 Mar 2025; comment 'under review LION19'). Report said 'small models with context can beat larger ones' - true for the pair Qwen2.5-Coder:32b (CEoH) vs GPT-4o (EoH), but the paper notes GPT-4o did better with plain EoH than with CEoH, so context does not always help. Parent set to eoh. Org confirmed from the arXiv HTML (review 2026-11-03).
